item.title: Balad: Disqualification petition against Abu Shehadeh is political persecution
item.description: Balad attacks Otzma Yehudit’s attempt to bar Sami Abu Shehadeh from running, calling it a "campaign of incitement and political persecution."

item.title: Heavy military movement: IDF and Home Front Command launch surprise drill across Israel
item.description: IDF and Home Front Command launch a surprise drill across Israel that will continue until the afternoon. Increased military activity is expected, but there is no security threat.

item.title: Air Canada investigates antisemitic social media posts by service director
item.description: Air Canada removes an in-flight service director from service and launches an investigation after antisemitic social media posts about Israel surfaced.

item.title: Report: Trump to meet Gulf leaders at UN to discuss Iran war
item.description: Axios reports Trump is expected to meet Gulf leaders at the UN next week to discuss the Iran war, postwar plans and the next steps for the region.

item.title: Israel, Morocco agree to upgrade ties, expand flights and exchange ambassadors
item.description: Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar meets Moroccan counterpart and the two agree to upgrade Israel-Morocco ties, expand flights and appoint ambassadors by the end of 2026.

item.title: Mamdani will not join protests against Netanyahu during UN visit
item.description: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani confirms he will not join UN protests against Benjamin Netanyahu while defending residents' constitutional right to demonstrate.

item.title: Poll: Netanyahu’s bloc takes lead
item.description: Likud loses another seat, falling to 18, while Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar remains in first place. Netanyahu’s coalition bloc rises to 54 seats, overtaking the Eisenkot bloc.

item.title: NY Times deletes line questioning Israeli victimhood on Oct. 7
item.description: The New York Times removes a sentence suggesting Israeli victimhood after Oct. 7 was a matter of perception, calling it an “editing error."

item.title: State Department confirms: Abbas denied a visa ahead of UN General Assembly
item.description: The State Department confirmed on Wednesday night that it has refused to issue entry visas to Palestinian Authority (PA) chairman Mahmoud Abbas and members of his delegation ahead of next week’s United Nations General Assembly in New York.
